relations.myth: Legba’s descending world-tree aspect bears the name Grand Bois
relations.note: Deren presents Grand Bois as Legba’s western, arboreal, underworld transformation.
Rigaud associates the ritual post with both Papa Loko and Maître Grand Bois.
Some houses understand Gran Bwa as Loko’s Petwo road or manifestation.
Other houses distinguish the spirits but say Gran Bwa and Loko walk together.
Deren places Grand Bois near Carrefour within her underworld cosmology.

relations.myth: Masters of woods, crossroads, and cemetery
relations.note: A song places Gran Bwa in woods and Mèt Kafou at crossroads.
Contemporary houses say they collaborate in magic or secret-society work.

relations.myth: Masters of woods, crossroads, and cemetery
relations.note: A song juxtaposes Gran Bwa in the woods with Bawon Lakwa in the cemetery.
Later systems group Gran Bwa, Kalfou, and Bawon Simityè as forest, roads, and death.
Deren links Grand Bois, Carrefour, and Ghede in an underworld movement.
Saint Sebastian’s tree-bound image serves as Gran Bwa’s Catholic visual counterpart.
relations.source: Vodou iconographic tables and practitioner accounts

relations.note: Modern comparative theology contrasts Osanyin’s leaf expertise with Gran Bwa’s total forest.
Modern teachings distinguish Gran Bwa’s forest from Gran Ibo’s swamp and plant wisdom.
